meaning: The number 22,000 appears in the Bible as the count of Levites who were numbered and dedicated to God's service as a replacement for Israel's firstborn, representing consecration, redemption, and divine service.
description: In Numbers 3:39, 22,000 Levites are counted as appointed to serve in the tabernacle. The Levites were given as a substitute for all the firstborn of Israel (Num 3:41), and thus the number 22,000 marks a people consecrated and dedicated to God's service. The firstborn who exceeded the number of Levites—273 individuals—had to be redeemed with silver money (Num 3:46–48), which underscores the central place of redemption in this narrative. Thus, the number 22,000 carries deep symbolism regarding election, substitutionary service, and consecration to the holy.

footnotes.text: The sum of the three Levitical clans listed in the text (Gershon 7,500, Kohath 8,600, Merari 6,200) gives 22,300, not 22,000. This discrepancy of 300 has been widely discussed. According to the Talmud (Bekhorot 5a), these 300 excess were themselves firstborn among the Levites and therefore could not redeem other firstborns, which explains why only 22,000 were counted.

In Jewish tradition, the number 22 holds special significance related to the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet, which in Kabbalistic thought are seen as the building blocks of creation (cf. Sefer Yetzirah). In this context, the number 22,000 can be understood as an amplification of this fundamental symbolism—the structure of creation manifested in a consecrated people.
